source.title: The Marginal Value of Adaptive Gradient Methods in Machine Learning
source.authors: Ashia C. Wilson; R. Roelofs; Mitchell Stern; N. Srebro; B. Recht

record.tranche_reason: This is the original study named for V4 and directly compares adaptive optimizers with SGD and momentum methods on natural data.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports a constructed binary classification example comparing adaptive methods with SGD; it is not a random-label memorization experiment. Hyperparameter values used only for tuning are not rows. Numerical results reported in figures are included only where the supplied text gives their values.
record.test_reason: This is the original source for V4. Its four deep-learning experiments compare adaptive optimizers with SGD and heavy-ball momentum while tuning learning rates and decay schedules.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase accurately reflects the authors' broad conclusion and tuning advice. Their evidence covers four tasks under learning-rate and decay tuning: SGD achieves the best held-out results, although RMSProp nearly matches it on character modeling and tuned Adam is close on discriminative parsing. The conclusion should not be read as establishing that adaptive methods are inferior across all machine-learning settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares standard adaptive methods with SGD and heavy-ball across constructed and deep-learning tasks; it uses tuned initial learning rates and decay schemes, with other hyperparameters generally left at defaults.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and task change the outcome; the adaptive methods show faster initial progress in some settings, while their development/test performance can plateau. Adam's default settings differ from tuned Adam. RMSProp closely trails SGD on War and Peace; AdaGrad trails substantially on the discriminative parser.

fits_no_version.finding: In a constructed overparameterized linear classification problem, adaptive methods interpolate using spurious features and approach error 1−p, whereas the minimum-norm solution found by non-adaptive methods approaches zero error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice can select interpolating linear classifiers with sharply different population errors on constructed separable data.

record.problems: The constructed example is stylized. The deep-learning experiments cover four tasks and use five random initializations per experiment. CIFAR-10 has no explicit development set, so settings were selected by training loss. Several exact values are supplied as figure annotations rather than described in prose.

untested.parts: Matched random-label memorization and natural-label generalization experiments.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and ordinary word-level language-model comparisons. Generative parsing models tree traversals rather than a standard word-level language benchmark.
Batch-size comparisons and changes to large-batch training recipes.
Controlled dropout comparisons and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay. The generative parser's dropout adjustment is not such an experiment.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.

missing.what: Training-versus-held-out comparisons needed to capture V4's better-training-performance clause: around epoch 50 on CIFAR-10, adaptive methods retain lower training error while SGD and HB begin achieving lower test error.

Default Adam achieves the best final training performance in discriminative parsing despite worse development performance; Adam also has one of the best training curves but the worst development perplexities in generative parsing. Existing rows record only held-out outcomes.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are assigned because this study is an original source for V4. Numerical held-out values match the supplied text. HB-only comparisons provide context but do not independently measure V4's adaptive-versus-non-adaptive contrast.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization using the same architecture and recipe.
Network width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptive large-batch recipes.
Dropout comparisons and interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: binary least-squares classification example
rows.size_stated: infinite dimensions; the text says dimensionality could be 6n
rows.operation_detail: Train AdaGrad on the constructed separable example; its solution labels all unseen data positive.
rows.baseline: SGD finds a solution with zero error on new data
rows.value: test errors arbitrarily close to half; the data-generating construction gives AdaGrad error 1 − p
rows.note: The theoretical construction compares optimizer solutions on a population with a discriminative feature and sparse, example-specific features.
rows.check: The constructed linear least-squares classifier is outside V4's image and language benchmark scope. Its subject_kind should describe a linear classifier. Error is 1−p on unseen examples; Appendix C gives conditional population error (1−p)(1−n/N), approaching 1−p as N grows.

rows.subject: binary least-squares classification example
rows.size_stated: infinite dimensions; the text says dimensionality could be 6n
rows.operation_detail: Train SGD on the constructed separable example.
rows.baseline: AdaGrad test error arbitrarily close to half in the construction
rows.value: zero test error; Appendix C bounds unconditional error above by n²/(2N)
rows.note: The paper states SGD learns a perfect classifier conditioned on no repeated training examples.
rows.check: The constructed linear classifier is outside V4's benchmark scope. Zero error in Section 3.3 requires n+ > n−/3; Appendix C reports zero conditional on no repeats and an unconditional upper bound n²/(2N), rather than unconditional zero.
